newsitem.title: USA: Lucent to buy Octel for $1.8 billion.
newsitem.headline: Lucent to buy Octel for $1.8 billion.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc. said Thursday it agreed to buy Octel Communications Corp. for $1.8 billion in a bid to beef up its voice mail, fax and messaging business in the United States and abroad.

Lucent, the telephone equipment maker that was spun off by AT&T Corp. last year, said the market for voice, fax and electronic messaging was now a $5 billion-a-year business that would probably double in size by 2000. The business is growing more than 20 percent a year, it said.
Under the deal, Lucent will pay $31 in cash for each Octel share. The company also said it will take a "significant" one-time charge against earnings related to the acquisition.
"This makes imminent sense. It think it is a fair price for Lucent and a good price for Octel shareholders," Salomon Bros. analyst Steve Levy said.
Octel stock jumped $3.375 to $30.125 on Nasdaq, while Lucent fell $2.625 to $86.06 on the New York Stock Exchange, largely because of the charge, traders and analysts said.
Lucent stock has been a Wall Street favourite during the current bull market, soaring from the initial public offering price of $27 in April 1996 when it was spun off from AT&T.
The deal will combine Octel technology, which works with many types of client systems, and Lucent's strong relationships with many phone companies.

Analysts noted that Octel is strong internationally, serving more than 140 telephone service providers in 70 countries, while Lucent is strongest in the United States. Octel also has strong relationships with many wireless providers, officials said.

In a conference call with reporters, the president of Lucent's business communications systems unit, Bill O'Shea, said the deal was "all about sustainable growth" and a "superior fit" between the two companies.

"Don't expect that this is going to be the final thing you hear about investing (by Lucent)," he said. But he declined to say what other acquisitions might be made by Lucent, which had nearly $1.5 billion in cash on hand as of June 30.
Octel founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Cohn will be president of the new messaging unit at Lucent.
Lucent said it expects to begin a cash tender offer for Octel on July 23 and close the deal late next month.
It said the charge will be taken in its fourth quarter ending in September, and will have a "significant" impact on earnings for the quarter and year. The company declined to provide more details.
Lucent, based in Murray Hill, N.J., said Wednesday that earnings nearly tripled to $213 million, or 33 cents a share, its third quarter, as sales rose 18 percent to $6.3 billion.
Octel, based in Milpitas, Calif., earned $10.6 million, or 20 cents a share, in its third quarter ended in April on sales of about $150 million. The company was founded in 1982.
The boards of both companies have approved the transaction, which is subject to approval by regulators.
